newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates slip on low demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates slip on low demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates slipped on Saturday amid dull trading as mill owners kept to the sidelines, waiting for a promised government relief package for the textile sector, dealers said.

"Cotton prices are under pressure on news that the government plans to announce a relief package for the ailing textile sector," dealer Kishan Chand said. "The buying tempo is slow and mill owners are in a wait-and-see mood."
He said sellers fear a ban on cotton exports as this year's cotton crop was lower than expectations. Kerb rates for NIAB-78 variety were around 2,150 rupees ($53.45) per maund (37.32 kg).
